skill.name: distributed-tracing
skill.description: Guides distributed tracing with Jaeger, Tempo, and OpenTelemetry to follow requests across microservices, analyze latency, and troubleshoot errors.
skill.summary: Guide distributed tracing setup and instrumentation for microservice observability.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly false positives caused by Markdown code fences, language examples, and visible example URLs in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, covert command execution, credential collection, or data exfiltration intent. Two production safety issues remain around sensitive trace metadata and unpinned container images.

remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to avoid raw SQL, user identifiers, tokens, and request bodies in span attributes. Recommend allow-listed, hashed, or redacted fields.
Replace latest image tags with explicit versions or digests for Jaeger and Tempo examples.
Add guidance for TLS, authentication, and network policy before using HTTP collector endpoints outside local examples.
Tell users to review remote manifests before applying them with kubectl, even when the source is an official release.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Data in Trace Attributes
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows recording database statements and recommends user_id tags in spans. Production trace stores can expose personal data or sensitive query details if copied without redaction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly include db.statement and user_id as trace metadata. These fields are common sources of sensitive data leakage in observability systems.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Observability Container Images
semantic_findings.description: The Docker Compose and Tempo examples use latest image tags. This creates nondeterministic deployments and can introduce unreviewed component changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited lines use latest tags for infrastructure images. This is a clear supply-chain hardening issue, though not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Distributed systems hide where latency and errors begin. This skill guides tracing setup, instrumentation, sampling, and analysis across services.
actual_capabilities: Explains trace, span, context, tag, and log concepts for request flow analysis.
Shows Jaeger deployment patterns for Kubernetes and Docker Compose.
Provides OpenTelemetry instrumentation examples for Python, Node.js, and Go services.
Demonstrates trace context propagation through HTTP headers and downstream calls.
Covers Tempo setup, sampling strategies, trace queries, and correlated logging.
Lists troubleshooting checks for missing traces and high tracing overhead.
limitations: Examples require adaptation for your cluster, language versions, and security controls.
The skill does not verify live Jaeger, Tempo, or collector deployments.
Referenced files are named, but this package only includes SKILL.md.
Production deployments still need TLS, authentication, retention, and privacy review.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Microservice Latency
use_cases.description: Trace a slow user request across gateway, service, and database spans.

use_cases.title: Standardize Tracing Rollout
use_cases.description: Create common OpenTelemetry patterns for several service teams.

use_cases.title: Correlate Errors With Logs
use_cases.description: Add trace IDs to logs so errors connect with full request paths.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Trace Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a request path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how one request should appear as spans for my service path: [describe services]. Include useful span names and safe attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me instrument a [Python Flask, Node.js Express, or Go] service for Jaeger. Use my service name: [name].

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Missing Traces
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tracing setup and list likely reasons traces do not appear in Jaeger or Tempo: [paste configuration summary].

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production tracing plan for [environment]. Include sampling, privacy controls, collector security, retention, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: A team asks why checkout requests take more than two seconds.
output: A service-by-service trace path that highlights the slow operation.
Suggested span attributes for latency analysis without sensitive data.
Checks for collector health, sampling rate, and database span duration.

output_examples.input: A developer wants downstream HTTP calls to stay in the same trace.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends injecting standard trace headers before the call and checking that child spans join the same trace.

output_examples.input: A platform owner needs Tempo sampling guidance.
output: A sampling approach for production traffic volume.
A reminder to protect trace storage and retention.
Troubleshooting steps for missing or delayed trace data.

best_practices: Use low production sampling rates unless business impact justifies higher trace volume.
Define an allow-list for span attributes, and exclude secrets, tokens, and personal data.
Pin collector endpoints, image versions, and storage settings per environment.
anti_patterns: Copying example endpoints into production without TLS, authentication, or network policy.
Recording raw request bodies, tokens, email addresses, or full SQL values in spans.
Using latest container tags for observability components in regulated environments.

faq.question: Does this skill install Jaeger or Tempo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup and instrumentation guidance. You decide which commands or manifests to apply.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The main examples cover Python, Node.js, and Go with OpenTelemetry.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Grafana Tempo?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Tempo configuration pattern and explains sampling and trace analysis.

faq.question: Will it solve missing traces automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives troubleshooting checks for endpoints, network connectivity, sampling, and application logs.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review TLS, authentication, retention, sampling, image pinning, and sensitive data controls.
